---
title: "Troubleshooting"
---

When a Positron session does not start, the cause is almost always in one of
three places: the install on the compute node, the license file, or the OOD
reverse proxy. This page is organized by symptom. Each section says where to
look and what the log shows.

## Where to look first

Every session has an output directory under the user's home directory:

```text
~/ondemand/data/sys/dashboard/batch_connect/sys/positron/output/<session-id>/
```

The **Session ID** link on the session card opens this directory in the OOD
file browser. `output.log` holds everything the job printed, including the
messages from `positron-server`. The directory also keeps the rendered
`script.sh` and `before.sh`, and `job_script_options.json` with the Slurm
options that OOD submitted.

A healthy start looks like this:

```text
Script starting...
Wed Oct 14 20:35:05 UTC 2026: Waiting for Positron Server to open port 25184...
TIMING - Starting main script at: Wed Oct 14 20:35:05 UTC 2026
Wed Oct 14 20:35:05 UTC 2026: Running on cpn01:25184
TIMING - Starting positron-server at: Wed Oct 14 20:35:05 UTC 2026
Server bound to 0.0.0.0:25184 (IPv4)
Extension host agent listening on 25184

Positron license verified: {"status":"activated", ...}
Verified license from license-manager directory.
Wed Oct 14 20:35:05 UTC 2026: Positron Server is listening on port 25184
```

After that, `positron-server` logs the extensions it unpacks on a first
start, then `Extension host agent started.` Messages about `vsda.js` and
`vsda_bg.wasm` not found are normal.

Errors in the form itself, before a job is submitted, go to the OOD
per-user log on the OOD host:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
tail -50 /var/log/ondemand-nginx/<username>/error.log
```

## The Positron tile does not appear

- **The app directory has the wrong name or location.** OOD lists every
  directory under `/var/www/ood/apps/sys/` that has a `manifest.yml`. Confirm
  `/var/www/ood/apps/sys/positron/manifest.yml` exists.
- **`cluster` in `form.yml` does not match a cluster file.** OOD hides an app
  whose cluster is not defined. The value must match a file name in
  `/etc/ood/config/clusters.d/`, without `.yml`.

## The form shows a 500 error

`form.yml` did not parse. Check the per-user log on the OOD host for the
line that names the problem, then fix the YAML. A common cause is a value
with a colon or a quote that is not quoted.

## The session stays in Starting, then disappears

`positron-server` exited before it opened the port, or right after. The
session card can show **Running** for a moment, because the server opens
the port before it checks the license. Open `output.log` and find the last
message from `positron-server`. The sections below cover the messages you
can see.

With this app, `after.sh` stops the job as soon as `positron-server` exits,
so the card goes away within a few seconds. On a job that stays in
**Starting** for the full 10 minutes, the server is running but the port
never opened. See [The port never opens](#the-port-never-opens).

### `positron-server: command not found`

The job did not find the server. Check, in this order:

1. `positron_server_dir` in `form.yml` is the directory that contains
   `bin/positron-server`, and every compute node mounts it.
2. If you use a module, `positron_module` names a module that exists on the
   compute nodes, and the module adds `bin` to `PATH`. The rendered
   `script.sh` in the session directory shows the exact `module load` line.
3. The compute node can run the binary. On the node, run
   `/opt/positron-server/bin/positron-server --version`.

### `script.sh: Permission denied`

`template/script.sh.erb` lost its execute bit, usually after a copy that did
not keep file modes. On the OOD host, run:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
chmod +x /var/www/ood/apps/sys/positron/template/script.sh.erb
```

## License errors

`positron-server` validates the license before it accepts connections. It
looks for `license.lic` in its activation directory,
`<install>/resources/activation/linux/<arch>/`, and runs the bundled
`license-manager` to check it. Check the license on a compute node first:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
/opt/positron-server/resources/activation/linux/<arch>/license-manager status
```

### `No license key provided`

```text
No license key provided. A license key is required to use Positron in a hosted
environment. Provide a license key with the --license-key or --license-key-file
command-line arguments, or set the POSITRON_LICENSE_KEY or
POSITRON_LICENSE_KEY_FILE environment variables.
```

Do not follow the advice in the message. It appears whenever
`positron-server` finds no usable license, and the command-line options it
names are for signed per-session keys that this app does not use. Check:

- **The file is missing.** `ls` the activation directory on a compute node.
  The file name must end in `.lic`.
- **The file is in the wrong architecture directory.** `positron-server`
  reads `linux/x86_64` on x86_64 nodes and `linux/aarch64` on ARM64 nodes.
  Both directories ship in every archive. `uname -m` on the node tells you
  which one it reads.
- **The install directory is not mounted on the compute node.** The install
  can be visible on the OOD host and absent on the node.

### `libcrypto.so.3` or `GLIBC_2.34` not found

```text
license-manager: error while loading shared libraries: libcrypto.so.3:
cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

```text
license-manager: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.34' not found
```

The bundled `license-manager` links against OpenSSL 3 and glibc 2.34. The
compute node runs an older release, so every license check fails and the
session log shows **No license key provided**. `positron-server` itself
needs only glibc 2.28, so the server starts, binds the port, and then
exits. Run the sessions on nodes with RHEL 9, Rocky Linux 9, Ubuntu 22.04,
or a newer release. RHEL 8 and Rocky Linux 8 do not meet the glibc
requirement, and a newer OpenSSL package alone does not fix it.

### `The license file next to the license-manager binary was rejected`

The file exists but `license-manager` did not accept it. The rest of the
line names the reason:

- **Permission denied**: each session reads the file as the user who
  launched it, so a root-only mode such as `600` fails every session. Set
  the mode to `644`.
- **License has expired**: ask Posit for a replacement file.
- **Invalid license result** or a signature error: the file was altered,
  or it is not a Positron Server license. Copy the file again from the
  original you received from Posit.

## The port never opens {#the-port-never-opens}

The session stays in **Starting** for 10 minutes, then disappears, and
`output.log` ends with:

```text
Timed out waiting for Positron Server to open port 25184
```

`after.sh` checks the port from the compute node itself, so a firewall is
not the cause here. The server is running but slow. The usual reasons:

- **The first start for a user.** `positron-server` unpacks its built-in
  extensions into `~/.positron-server` the first time. On a slow home
  filesystem this can take several minutes. Later starts are faster.
- **Too little memory.** Look for `oom-kill` in `output.log` or in the Slurm
  job record with `sacct -j <jobid> -o State,MaxRSS`. Raise the memory
  request. Positron Server needs at least 2.5 GB.
- **`shuf`, `ss`, and `lsof` are all missing on the node.** OOD uses them to
  find and check the port. `after.sh` cannot see the port without one of
  them. Install `iproute` for `ss`.

To give slow nodes more time, raise the `600` in `template/after.sh`.

## Connect to Positron shows an error or a blank page

The session is **Running**, but the new tab does not show Positron.

- **OOD shows "Not Found" or its own 404 page.** The `/rnode/` reverse proxy
  is off. Set `rnode_uri: "/rnode"` in `/etc/ood/config/ood_portal.yml`,
  run `update_ood_portal`, and restart Apache. See
  [Turn on the reverse proxy](get_started.qmd#turn-on-the-reverse-proxy).
- **OOD shows "Proxy Error" or a 502.** The OOD host could not reach the
  compute node on the session port. Either the session ended, or a firewall
  blocks the port range between the OOD host and the compute nodes. From the
  OOD host, run `curl -s http://<node>:<port>/` with the values from the
  session card. OOD picks a port between 2000 and 65535 by default.
- **The host name is rejected.** `host_regex` in `ood_portal.yml` does not
  match the node name that the session card shows. Change the pattern so it
  matches every compute node.
- **The tab shows `403 Forbidden`.** The address has no `tkn` parameter. This
  happens when a user copies the address without the token, or after the
  token cookie expires. Use the **Connect to Positron** button again.
- **The tab stays blank with no error.** The browser blocked the pop-up, or
  the page is still loading its assets through the proxy. Allow pop-ups for
  the OOD host and reload the tab.

## R or Python does not appear in the console

Positron finds interpreters on the `PATH` of the server process, and in the
usual install locations. The session has the `PATH` of a login shell on the
compute node, plus `positron_server_dir/bin`. Load the R and Python modules
you want in `template/script.sh.erb`, before the server starts, or install
them in a location Positron scans, such as `/usr/bin` or `/opt/R`.

Python also needs the `ipykernel` package. Positron ships a bundled copy
and uses it when the interpreter has none.

The interpreter picker shows **Discovering interpreters...** while Positron
looks for R and Python. The R extension writes what it found, and why it
rejected an install, to a log under the user's home directory on the
compute node:

```text
~/.local/state/positron/logs/<timestamp>/exthost*/positron.positron-r/R Language Pack.log
```

A log with no `Candidate R binary` line means discovery did not run. A
`Filtering out` line names the install and the reason, such as a version
below the minimum Positron supports.

## Slow start

- A first session for a user takes longer. See
  [The port never opens](#the-port-never-opens).
- Sessions on a busy partition wait in **Queued** until Slurm has a node.
  `squeue -u <username>` shows the reason.
- Inside Apptainer, the first start also unpacks the image. Put the `.sif`
  file on a fast local or parallel filesystem, not on NFS over a slow link.

## Still stuck?

Open an issue at
[the positron-server-ood issue tracker](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-server-ood/issues)
with `output.log` from the session directory, your Positron Server version,
your OOD version, and the operating system of the compute nodes.
